methodology.cold_process_isolation: The runner starts one new benchmark process for every sample.
methodology.warm_preparation: Warm cases perform their documented preparation before the timed interval; preparation is never included as a sample.
methodology.threshold_policy: Absolute ceilings are version controlled here and cannot be overridden by the runner. A missing ceiling is a gate failure.
methodology.threshold_tolerance_policy: A statistic above its ceiling but no higher than ceiling x (1 + threshold_tolerance) passes and is reported as a warning; a higher one fails. The runner pins the tolerance, so this file alone cannot widen it. The band absorbs hosted-runner variation: over 37 CI runs from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-16, javascript_wrapped_core_ratio ranged from 0.79 to 1.05 of its ceilings, and byte-identical binaries measured a median of 547 in one run and 617 in another (#463).
methodology.reference_hardware: The ceilings are calibrated on the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 x86-64 runners of CI extended, and the CI result is the reference. There the other microsecond ceilings leave at least 2.4 times headroom, while javascript_wrapped_core leaves about 1.2 times, so a run on slower hardware can exceed it without a regression: a quiet Arm Neoverse-N1 machine measured a median of 6234 us (#465). Reports record the CPU model and the runner environment.
methodology.memory_definition: Primitive cases use the QuickJS custom allocator high-water mark. Program and Core cases use the fresh process resident-set high-water mark.
methodology.core_pair_order: Enabled and disabled binaries alternate first position by sample index.

ab_comparison.policy: When a base build is given (verify_ci.py quickjs-performance --base <ref>), every primitive and control case except replay_growth also runs on it, alternating base and head samples by sample index on the same machine. The ratio of the head median to the base median warns above warning_ratio. A blocking case above failure_ratio is compared once more with fresh samples and fails only if that comparison is above failure_ratio too. A case the base build does not have is reported as skipped. The absolute ceilings still apply. Hosted runner types differ by more than these ratios, so only a comparison on one machine can see a regression of 10-25% (#476).

cases.scope: JS_NewRuntime2 plus JS_NewContext in a fresh process
global source compile-only after fresh runtime creation
ES module compile-only after fresh runtime creation
JavaScript module compile, define evaluation, builder validation, and strict Core lowering
first next() on an already-open generator yielding a canonical literal command
per-command next(response) after one discarded generator step
ng.callCore construction plus canonical C++ response conversion and next command
fresh-process resident-set high-water mark after lowering a representative 64-node builder
sealed JavaScript generator yielding two sequential admitted Core commands through the in-memory ProgramRuntime
sealed JavaScript ng.all command joining two admitted Core commands through the in-memory ProgramRuntime
sealed JavaScript ng.race command joining two admitted Core commands through the in-memory ProgramRuntime
sealed JavaScript ng.quorum command joining two admitted Core commands through the in-memory ProgramRuntime
sealed JavaScript ng.await command wrapping one admitted Core command through the in-memory ProgramRuntime
per-invocation time of 128 repeated JavaScript generator plus in-memory ProgramRuntime Core invocations after one warm-up invocation; the numerator of javascript_wrapped_core_ratio
cases.threshold_basis: Set from the javascript_wrapped_core_us component of javascript_wrapped_core_ratio, which times the same run, in 39 hosted-runner measurements in CI extended from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-16 (#465). Run medians ranged from 2436 to 4515 us (3967 to 4515 us on the slower runner class), run p95s reached 4720 us and run MADs 60 us. The median ceiling is 1.22 times the highest run median and the p95 ceiling 1.27 times the highest run p95.

cases.scope: 128 repeated JavaScript generator plus in-memory ProgramRuntime Core invocations divided by direct Core invocation; repeated denominator timing suppresses sub-10us clock noise. Reported, not blocking: a faster Core alone raises the ratio and a slower one can hide a slower JavaScript path, so javascript_wrapped_core gates the wrapped run's own time (#465)

Core runtime with QuickJS enabled but unlinked/unused divided by an otherwise identical disabled build; each paired process averages 4096 Core invocations to suppress microsecond-scale scheduler jitter

fresh QuickJS source re-execution at each recorded command count, requiring canonical equality of every yielded command against an immutable pre-recorded stream; excludes ProgramRuntime scheduling, journal I/O, and Core dispatch
